## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. The S&P 500 closed Tuesday at its lowest level since July 29, its fourth straight loss. Rate-hike worries are hitting gold and bitcoin hardest, and a strong Nvidia report hasn't turned sentiment around.

## 2. What moved and why
**Stocks stay under pressure despite a strong Nvidia report**
Why it happened: Nvidia beat estimates, but its early gain faded after the open. Software and retail losses dragged on the Dow.
Why it matters: The S&P 500 is sitting on a key technical line, so a clean break could pull in more selling.

**Gold sinks to its lowest level in over a year**
Why it happened: A stronger US dollar and rising expectations of higher Fed rates are weighing on the metal. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that another hike will likely be needed.
Why it matters: Gold pays no interest, so higher real yields and a firmer dollar make it less attractive.

**Bitcoin slides further as rate bets and ETF outflows bite**
Why it happened: Wintermute links the drop to higher rate expectations, weak ETF demand and $1.7B in liquidations.
Why it matters: Bitcoin is trading well below key long-term averages, and sentiment is deeply fearful.

## Deals
- **IPO: Anthropic → public markets: Anthropic** (Size: not disclosed in the sources I found.). Investors are waiting for final pricing, and trading is expected to start Thursday. It is a test of IPO appetite for AI companies in a shaky tape.

data.headline: Stocks slide as rate-hike fears hit gold, bitcoin

stories.title: Stocks stay under pressure despite a strong Nvidia report
stories.why_happened: Nvidia beat estimates, but its early gain faded after the open. Software and retail losses dragged on the Dow.
stories.why_matters: The S&P 500 is sitting on a key technical line, so a clean break could pull in more selling.
stories.full: The S&P 500 was down 3.2% over the month through Tuesday. Investors are unsure about the AI trade, and a scandal at Nvidia led to CEO Jensen Huang's departure. Nvidia's report was the first test since that exit. Revenue was $107.6B against a consensus of $101.87B, and the Q4 revenue guide of $130B is about 4% above expectations. Other chipmakers such as AMD jumped. Nvidia's own shares still gave back their gains. The Dow fell by more than 1%. The S&P 500 ended Tuesday at 7,340.53, just under its 200-day average of 7,346.64. BTIG's technician says the next stop could be the 7,000–7,100 zone. Bulls counter that hyperscalers haven't cut their capex plans and compute demand remains solid. Chip suppliers and AI infrastructure names are the winners so far. Software and rate-sensitive growth stocks are the losers. Watch the 2:00 PM Fed minutes and Palo Alto Networks' results tonight.

stories.why_happened: A stronger US dollar and rising expectations of higher Fed rates are weighing on the metal. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that another hike will likely be needed.
stories.why_matters: Gold pays no interest, so higher real yields and a firmer dollar make it less attractive.
stories.full: Gold fell below $3,800 on Wednesday, its lowest in about 14 months, as rate-hike bets lifted the dollar. The dollar is near a 19-month high, which makes gold costlier for buyers using other currencies. The slide is the opposite of a classic safe-haven move. Gold is roughly 33% below its January record of $5,595. Yahoo Finance, citing CME FedWatch, put the chance of a December rate increase at 96.7%. The next Fed decision is on December 9. Miners, including Canadian gold producers, lose from lower prices. Importers and dollar holders gain. The World Gold Council flags $3,605 as potential support. Watch the minutes this afternoon for how firmly the Fed leans toward another hike.

stories.why_matters: Bitcoin is trading well below key long-term averages, and sentiment is deeply fearful.
stories.full: Bitcoin is around 26% below its October high after crashing toward $62,000 over the weekend. It closed below its 200-week moving average near $68K. It also failed to follow stock futures higher after Nvidia's beat. The popular basis trade now yields only about 3–5% a year, near or below Treasury yields. That removes a source of steady demand. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 11, in extreme fear. Leveraged long holders and ETF buyers are the losers. Strategy's average purchase price was $75,451 on 849,327 BTC, so its position is underwater. Wintermute warns that a drop below $60,000 is possible. Watch ETF flows and whether the 200-week line can be reclaimed.

intern.headline: Stocks slide as rate-hike fears hit gold, bitcoin
intern.mood: Nervous. The S&P 500 (a basket of 500 big US companies, used as a market gauge) closed Tuesday at its lowest level since July 29. That is its fourth straight loss. Fears of higher interest rates are hitting gold and bitcoin hardest. A strong report from Nvidia (a company that makes chips for AI) has not turned the mood around.

stories.title: Stocks stay under pressure despite a strong Nvidia report
stories.why_happened: Nvidia beat estimates (beat expectations set by analysts), but its early gain faded after the market opened. Software and retail stocks pulled down the Dow (an index of 30 big US companies).
stories.why_matters: The S&P 500 is sitting on a key chart line (a moving average, which is a line showing the typical price over time). If it breaks below that line cleanly, more selling could follow.
stories.full: The S&P 500 was down 3.2% over the month through Tuesday. Investors are unsure about the AI trade (bets on companies that use artificial intelligence to grow). A scandal at Nvidia led to the departure of its CEO, Jensen Huang. Nvidia's report was the first test since he left. Revenue was $107.6B, above the $101.87B that analysts expected (the consensus). Its guidance (its forecast) for Q4 revenue is $130B, about 4% above what people expected. Other chip companies such as AMD jumped. Nvidia's own shares still gave back their gains. The Dow fell by more than 1%. The S&P 500 ended Tuesday at 7,340.53. That is just under its 200-day average of 7,346.64 (the average price over the last 200 trading days). BTIG's technician, an analyst who studies price charts, says the next stop could be the 7,000 to 7,100 zone. Bulls (investors who expect prices to rise) argue that big tech companies have not cut their spending on computing plans, and demand for computing power is still solid. Chip suppliers and AI infrastructure companies are the winners so far. Software companies and growth stocks that are sensitive to interest rates are the losers. Watch the Fed minutes (notes from the central bank's last meeting) at 2:00 PM and Palo Alto Networks' results tonight.

stories.title: Gold sinks to its lowest level in over a year
stories.why_happened: A stronger US dollar and rising expectations of higher Fed interest rates are pushing gold down. New York Fed President John Williams said on Tuesday that another rate hike will likely be needed.
stories.why_matters: Gold pays no interest. When real yields (interest rates after inflation) rise and the dollar gets stronger, gold becomes less attractive to hold.
stories.full: Gold fell below $3,800 on Wednesday. That is its lowest level in about 14 months. Bets on rate hikes lifted the dollar. The dollar is near a 19-month high, which makes gold more expensive for buyers who use other currencies. This slide is the opposite of a classic safe-haven move (when investors run to gold during trouble). Gold is roughly 33% below its January record of $5,595. Yahoo Finance, citing CME FedWatch (a tool that tracks market bets on Fed moves), put the chance of a rate increase in December at 96.7%. The next Fed decision is on December 9. Gold miners, including Canadian gold producers, lose when prices fall. Importers and people who hold dollars gain. The World Gold Council flags $3,605 as a possible support level (a price where buyers may step in). Watch the Fed minutes this afternoon for how strongly the Fed leans toward another rate hike.

stories.title: Bitcoin slides further as rate bets and ETF outflows bite
stories.why_happened: Wintermute (a crypto trading firm) links the drop to higher rate expectations, weak demand through ETFs (funds that trade like stocks and hold bitcoin), and $1.7B in liquidations (forced sales of bets that went wrong).
stories.why_matters: Bitcoin is trading well below key long-term averages, and investor mood is very fearful.
stories.full: Bitcoin is around 26% below its October high. It crashed toward $62,000 over the weekend. It closed below its 200-week moving average (a long-term price average) near $68K. It also failed to follow stock futures higher after Nvidia's beat. The popular basis trade (a strategy that earns a small profit from the gap between bitcoin prices in two markets) now yields only about 3 to 5% a year. That is near or below Treasury yields (the interest paid on US government bonds). This removes a source of steady demand. The Fear & Greed Index (a score of investor mood from 0 to 100) sits at 11, which is extreme fear. Leveraged long holders (investors who borrowed money to bet on prices rising) and ETF buyers are the losers. Strategy's average purchase price was $75,451 on 849,327 BTC. That means its position is underwater, worth less than it paid. Wintermute warns that a drop below $60,000 is possible. Watch ETF flows and whether bitcoin can get back above the 200-week line.

deals.type: IPO (Initial Public Offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public)
deals.value: Not disclosed in the sources I found
deals.why: Investors are waiting for final pricing, and trading is expected to start Thursday. It is a test of how much appetite (demand) investors have for AI companies while markets are shaky.
deals.full: The offering is being called a marquee deal (a big, high-profile deal), and it is arriving just as the AI trade wobbles. I could not find the number of shares, the price range, the valuation (the company's total worth) or the underwriters (the banks running the sale). Check the final prospectus (the official document about the sale) and the pricing release for those details. A stock listing gives an AI company access to deep public money for its computing spending. It also lets early holders sell their shares. If the final price lands within, above or below the expected range, people will read that as a sign of how much investors want AI stocks. Watch for any upsizing (selling more shares than planned), the first-day move, and the lock-up terms (the rules that stop insiders from selling for a set period).

glossary.meaning: When the central bank raises its key interest rate to slow the economy and fight rising prices.
The interest rate an investment pays, shown as a percentage of its price.
An investment that people buy when they are scared, hoping it will hold its value.
A fund that holds a basket of assets, like bitcoin or stocks, and trades on an exchange like a single stock.
When a broker forces the sale of a borrowed bet because its value fell too far.
The first time a private company sells its shares to the public on a stock exchange.
